text: Question: A female client tells the nurse that she is quite sure she is pregnant. Which of the following is a positive sign of pregnancy?
C. HCG detected in the urine.
notes: Correct: “Fetal heartbeat” – This is a positive sign.
• “Uterine enlargement” – This is a probable sign.
• “HCG detected in the urine” – This is a probable sign.

slides.title: The nurse is assessing a pregnant client with a diagnosis of abruptio placentae.
text: Question: The nurse is assessing a pregnant client with a diagnosis of abruptio placentae. Which of the following should the nurse expect to assess on the client? Select all that apply.
D. Abdominal and lower back pain.
Correct answers: A. Uterine irritability.; B. Uterine tenderness.; D. Abdominal and lower back pain.; F. Nonreassuring fetal heart patterns.
notes: • “Bright red vaginal bleeding” – Dark red bleeding.
• “Strong and frequent contractions” – Frequent low intensity contractions.

slides.title: A 26-year-old primigravida client at 4 weeks gestation arrives at the outpatient
text: Question: A 26-year-old primigravida client at 4 weeks gestation arrives at the outpatient clinic for an initial prenatal visit. Which of the following findings would be consistent with the client’s history? Select all that apply.
Correct answers: A. Fatigue.; B. Nausea.; D. Breast sensitivity.
notes: Early pregnancy (presumptive signs) includes fatigue, nausea, and breast tenderness. Quickening is first felt around 16–20 weeks (earlier in multiparas), and Braxton Hicks contractions appear in the second and third trimesters.
